rv.q: There’s a considerable amount to admire in this production , but it is ultimately something of a hollow edifice.

His legacy, however much he likes to think of himself as having achieved great and marvellous things, is a bunch of amateurs, who would only be professionals if they went off and achieved the relevant qualifications elsewhere. Greg Hicks in The Master Builder.

Robert Innes Hopkins’ set places the production firmly in the 21st-century design world of demanding clients, big egos, and office politics. When Halvard Solness enters, the picture is complete. He is a charismatic, successful, demanding, senior architect in every way: a fully recognizable type.
Ultimately, The Master Builder succeeds through its compelling performances, above all Binder’s mesmerising and unsettling portrayal of Hilde.

cn.t: Strong central performances anchor this psychologically compelling but slow-burning Ibsen revival, though the unsympathetic characters and befuddling narrative may leave audiences cold.
